title: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.CondensedRing.boundedConstructible_tateTwistDerived
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and let $X$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $d,n\in\mathbf Z$. Write $B=\mathrm{Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj}(\ell)$ for the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}}_\ell$ [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and $B_X=p_X^*B$ for its coefficient ring on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Use exactly the internal-module Tate construction $B_X(d)$ of [def-pur-condensed-tate-twists], and let $\mathrm{tateTwistDerived}(X,\ell,d)=B_X(d)[0]$. Then
$$\mathrm{tateTwistDerived}(X,\ell,d)[n]\in D^b_c(X)[[B]],$$
where bounded constructibility is exactly the upstream predicate boundedConstructible, i.e. [def-sfb-bounded-constructible-complexes] (the definition recorded for the blueprint unit [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]) in the ordinary unbounded derived category of internal $B_X$-modules: cohomology is zero outside a finite interval, and every cohomology module is constructible in the sense of [def-sfb-constructible-module], namely there is one finite stratification of $X$ by immersions $g_a\colon X_a\to X$ such that each $g_a^*$ of the module is locally finitely presented over $g_a^*B_X$. No quasi-compactness, Noetherianity, finite-type or finite-field hypothesis on $X$ is assumed. The invertibility hypothesis repairs the unrestricted upstream lemma; it is the hypothesis of the blueprint Tate-twist setting [sk-def-sp-tate-twist].

proof.text: Put $R_X=p_X^*\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell$ and $A_{r,X}=(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_X$ for $r\ge1$. At $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] gives $R_X\simeq\varprojlim_r A_{r,X}$, compatibly with scheme inverse image and the coefficient maps. Apply [lem-pur-condensed-zl-reduction-mod-ell-power] on this same scheme $X$: its quotient isomorphism $R_X/\ell^rR_X\simeq A_{r,X}$ is an isomorphism of rings and $R_X$-modules, and its compatibility clause identifies successive quotient maps with the reduction maps $A_{r+1,X}\to A_{r,X}$. The helper requires only a prime and a scheme, so imposes no extra hypothesis on $X$. These are precisely the coefficient identifications used in the next two steps.

source.place: Integral limit and coefficient extension; spell out the quotient comparison needed to identify the exact upstream Tate construction

proof.text: Write $F_r=R_X\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mu_{\ell^r,X}$ for the actual free internal-module level in [def-pur-condensed-tate-twists]. Since $\ell^r$ annihilates the abelian sheaf $\mu_{\ell^r,X}$, balancing factors its tensor through $R_X/\ell^r R_X=A_{r,X}$ from Step 1. Thus the maps $a\otimes z\mapsto az$ and $z\mapsto1\otimes z$ are inverse $R_X$-linear maps $F_r\simeq\mu_{\ell^r,X}$. The first composite sends $z$ to $z$; the other sends $a\otimes z$ to $1\otimes az=a\otimes z$, because the reduction of $a$ in the constant sheaf $A_{r,X}$ is locally represented by an integer $k$, and locally $1\otimes az=1\otimes kz=k\otimes z=a\otimes z$. These local equalities give equality of the sheaf maps. For the transition from $r+1$ to $r$, the two composites on $a\otimes z$ give $\bar a\cdot(z^\ell)$ and $(a\cdot z)^\ell$, which agree: after reducing $a$ modulo $\ell^{r+1}$, choose locally an integer representative $k$ of that residue section; both are then $z^{k\ell}$. Here $\bar a$ is reduction modulo $\ell^r$. This agrees with the transition because it is $1\otimes(z\mapsto z^\ell)$ and the scalar quotient maps are the reduction maps. The level $r=0$ is zero since $\mu_1$ is the trivial abelian sheaf. A cone over the positive levels extends uniquely by the zero map to this level. Therefore the limit universal property, applied to these compatible inverse maps, identifies the actual $T_X=\varprojlim_{r\ge0}F_r$ with $Z_X=\varprojlim_{r\ge1}\mu_{\ell^r,X}$ as an $R_X$-module.

source.place: Displayed roots-of-unity inverse limit; identify all levels, their transitions and the harmless level zero

proof.text: Apply clause 2 of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] with $S=X$ and $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Its hypotheses require precisely that $\ell$ be invertible on $X$. It supplies a pro-etale covering $V_j\to X$ with $Z_X|_{V_j}\simeq\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,V_j}$. Step 1 identifies these rings with $R_{V_j}$. The actual positive Tate line is $L_X=B_X\otimes_{R_X}T_X$ by [def-pur-condensed-tate-twists]. Restricting this sheaf tensor to the covering slice keeps the same sectionwise tensor and sheafification, hence on $V_j$ it becomes $B_{V_j}\otimes_{R_{V_j}}R_{V_j}$. Multiplication $b\otimes r\mapsto br$ and $b\mapsto b\otimes1$ identify this with $B_{V_j}$. The coefficient comparisons in [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] identify the restricted rings with these displayed coefficient rings. Thus the actual upstream line, rather than a line in a rationalized category, is locally free of rank one.

source.place: Each coefficient Tate line is locally free of rank one; use the integral line and the exact scalar extension

proof.text: Use the very same covering of Step 3. The signed powers in [def-pur-condensed-tate-twists] give $B_X(0)|_{V_j}=B_{V_j}$. Inductively the positive powers restrict to $B_{V_j}\otimes_{B_{V_j}}B_{V_j}\simeq B_{V_j}$, with inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. For a negative power the definition is the sheaf Hom into $B_X$ of the corresponding positive power. On the covering slice, [def-pur-sheaf-hom] describes it as the sheaf of module maps out of $B_{V_j}$; evaluation at $1$ identifies it with $B_{V_j}$, with inverse sending a section $b$ to multiplication by $b$. Restriction to a smaller object commutes with these formulas. This proves that $B_X(d)$ is pro-etale locally free of rank one for every integer $d$, including zero and negative integers.

source.place: Tensor powers and dual powers; write the zero and negative cases explicitly

proof.text: Each local trivialization in Step 4 is a finite constant local model: choose the scalar module $P=B(*)=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with presentation $B(*)^0\to B(*)^1\to P\to0$. Extending this presentation to $B_{V_j}$ gives $0\to B_{V_j}$ with cokernel $B_{V_j}$; the matrix has zero columns and scalar entries. This satisfies both the scalar-model criterion and its local finite-presentation consequence in [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Use the one-stratum stratification $X=X$; its immersion is the identity and its image is constructible (the entire space). The definition [sk-def-sfb-constructible] now gives constructibility of $B_X(d)$. This argument also gives the global finite-stratification predicate in the exact upstream source, without relying on the weaker affine-local convention: the single stratum works on the whole scheme. For the zero sheaf use $P=0$ and the rank-zero presentation. The covering itself need not be a finite family. Explicitly for the predicate of [def-sfb-constructible-module]: take the stratification with the single stratum $g=\mathrm{id}_X$, so $g^*$ is the identity up to the canonical isomorphism and $g^*B_X=B_X$. For each member $u_j\colon V_j\to X$ of the pro-etale covering of Step 4, the pullback $u_j^*$ of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star] is restriction to the slice $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/V_j=(V_j)_{\mathrm{proet}}$: the base change functor $W\mapsto W\times_XV_j$ has as left adjoint the functor regarding a $V_j$-object as an $X$-object, so the left Kan extension along it is precomposition with that left adjoint, which is already a sheaf. Hence $\operatorname{mapMod}(u_j^*)B_X(d)\simeq B_{V_j}=\operatorname{coker}(B_{V_j}^0\to B_{V_j}^1)$ is finitely presented [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module], so $B_X(d)$ is locally finitely presented [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented] and constructible; the zero module is $\operatorname{coker}(B_X^0\to B_X^0)$.

source.place: Rank-one local model implies constructibility; one stratum suffices on arbitrary schemes

proof.text: By [def-pur-condensed-tate-twists], $\mathrm{tateTwistDerived}(X,\ell,d)$ is represented by the complex with $B_X(d)$ in degree zero, zero in all other degrees and all differentials zero. Its shift by $n$ has that same sheaf in degree $-n$, zero elsewhere and zero differentials. The kernel/image formula for cohomology gives $H^{-n}=B_X(d)$ and $H^i=0$ for $i\ne-n$. Both kinds of cohomology sheaf are constructible by Step 5, and the interval $[-n,-n]$ is a single bound independent of $X$. This is exactly the predicate [def-sfb-bounded-constructible-complexes] (the predicate named by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]). No assertion that the entire bounded constructible subcategory is triangulated is needed. The calculation also covers empty $X$, when all the displayed module sheaves are zero.
